Integrate your Apollo Router with Dynatrace to gain visibility into your GraphQL infrastructure through distributed tracing, metrics, and pre-built dashboards.

## Recommended setup flow

1. **Choose a connection method** (this page): Decide between direct OTLP export and an OpenTelemetry Collector
1. **[Configure the metrics exporter](/graphos/routing/observability/router-telemetry-otel/apm-guides/dynatrace/dynatrace-metrics)**: Send router metrics to Dynatrace over OTLP
1. **[Configure the trace exporter](/graphos/routing/observability/router-telemetry-otel/apm-guides/dynatrace/dynatrace-traces)**: Send router spans to Dynatrace over OTLP
1. **[Create a dashboard](/graphos/routing/observability/router-telemetry-otel/apm-guides/dynatrace/dashboard-template)**: Import Apollo's pre-configured Dynatrace dashboard template

## Connection methods

Choose one of the following methods based on your infrastructure:

- **Direct OTLP/HTTP export**: The router exports metrics and traces straight to your Dynatrace environment's OTLP endpoints. Fewest moving parts, and the router produces delta metrics itself. This method cannot ship router logs (see [Router logs](#router-logs)).
- **[OpenTelemetry collector](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/collector/)**: The router exports OTLP to a collector, and the collector forwards to Dynatrace with an `otlphttp` exporter. Use this method to keep Dynatrace credentials out of the router config, fan out to more than one backend, or ship router logs by tailing the router's stdout with a `filelog` receiver. If the collector receives cumulative metrics, its metrics pipeline must include the [`cumulativetodelta` processor](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/processor/cumulativetodeltaprocessor).
- **ActiveGate or Dynatrace Managed**: When the router has no direct route to the internet, an [ActiveGate](https://docs.dynatrace.com/docs/extend-dynatrace/opentelemetry/getting-started/otlp-export) provides a local ingest endpoint, playing a role similar to a local agent in other APM stacks. Only the endpoint's host and path prefix change:

| Deployment | Endpoint shape |
|---|---|
| SaaS | `https://{env-id}.live.dynatrace.com:443/api/v2/otlp/v1/{signal}` |
| Managed | `https://{your-domain}:443/e/{env-id}/api/v2/otlp/v1/{signal}` |
| ActiveGate | `https://{activegate-host}:9999/e/{env-id}/api/v2/otlp/v1/{signal}` |

## Configuration requirements

Dynatrace's OTLP ingest has several hard requirements. Most misconfigurations produce no router error—the export appears to succeed while the data never arrives—so verify each of these:

- **Temporality must be `delta`** on the metrics exporter. Dynatrace accepts cumulative metrics with a 2xx response and then silently drops them.
- **Protocol must be `http`** on every signal. Dynatrace doesn't support gRPC ingest, and an omitted `protocol` defaults to gRPC, so the exporter fails to connect.
- **Each signal has its own endpoint path**: `/api/v2/otlp/v1/metrics`, `/api/v2/otlp/v1/traces`, and `/api/v2/otlp/v1/logs`. A mismatched path—for example, the traces path on the metrics exporter—can be accepted and then discarded.
- **Include the port explicitly.** If your endpoint host doesn't contain a port, append `:443`.
- **The `Authorization` header value starts with `Api-Token`**, not `Bearer`. A `Bearer` token returns 401s that surface only in exporter logs.
- **Configure one exporter per signal.** Metrics, traces, and logs are separate exporters in `telemetry.exporters`; enabling one does nothing for the others.
- **Unset the `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` environment variables** (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT`). In router v2.12 and earlier they silently override the YAML telemetry configuration; v2.13 and later refuses to start.

## Minimal configuration

The following configuration exports metrics and traces directly to Dynatrace. Set `DYNATRACE_ENV_URL` (for example, `https://abc12345.live.dynatrace.com:443`) and `DYNATRACE_API_TOKEN` in the router's environment.

```yaml title="router.yaml"
telemetry:
  exporters:
    metrics:
      common:
        service_name: apollo-router
      otlp:
        enabled: true
        protocol: http            # Dynatrace doesn't support gRPC ingest
        temporality: delta        # required; cumulative metrics are dropped
        endpoint: ${env.DYNATRACE_ENV_URL}/api/v2/otlp/v1/metrics
        http:
          headers:
            Authorization: "Api-Token ${env.DYNATRACE_API_TOKEN}"
    tracing:
      common:
        service_name: apollo-router
        sampler: 0.05             # sample well below 1.0 in production
      otlp:
        enabled: true
        protocol: http
        endpoint: ${env.DYNATRACE_ENV_URL}/api/v2/otlp/v1/traces
        http:
          headers:
            Authorization: "Api-Token ${env.DYNATRACE_API_TOKEN}"
    logging:
      stdout:
        enabled: true
        format: json
```

<Note>

Reference the token with `${env.DYNATRACE_API_TOKEN}` (or `${file.}`) rather than inlining it in `router.yaml`.

</Note>

## Router logs

The router has no OTLP log exporter—`telemetry.exporters.logging` supports only `common` and `stdout`, and a `logging.otlp` key prevents the router from starting. To get router logs into Dynatrace, emit JSON logs to stdout (as in the configuration above) and forward them with a log shipper: an OpenTelemetry Collector `filelog` receiver, or an existing host forwarder such as OneAgent log ingestion.

## API tokens

Dynatrace uses different token types for ingest and for the platform APIs. Using one where the other is expected returns a 401.

| Purpose | Header | Token type and scopes |
|---|---|---|
| OTLP ingest (metrics, traces, logs) | `Authorization: Api-Token dt0c01...` | Access token with `metrics.ingest`, `openTelemetryTrace.ingest`, `logs.ingest` |
| Dashboard import | `Authorization: Bearer dt0s16...` | Platform token with `document:documents:write` |
